translation_en: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Numayr, and Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Zayd ibn Hubab narrated to us, from al-Dahhak ibn ‘Uthman, from Bukayr ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Ashajj, from Sulayman ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever buys food must not sell it until he has measured it.” Abu Bakr’s narration says, “Whoever purchases.”

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Harith al-Makhzumi narrated to us: al-Dahhak ibn ‘Uthman narrated to us, from Bukayr ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Ashajj, from Sulayman ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said to Marwan, “You have permitted the sale of usury.” Marwan said, “I have not done that.” Abu Hurayrah said, “You permitted the sale of food vouchers, but the Messenger of Allah forbade selling food until it has been fully received.” Marwan then addressed the people and forbade their sale. Sulayman said: I saw guards taking them from people’s hands.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: Rawh narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us: Abu al-Zubayr narrated to me that he heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah say: The Messenger of Allah used to say: “When you buy food, do not sell it until you have fully received it.”

Abu al-Tahir Ahmad ibn ‘Amr ibn Sarh informed me: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj narrated to me, that Abu al-Zubayr informed him: I heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah say: The Messenger of Allah forbade selling a heap of dates whose measure was unknown for a specified measure of dates.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Rawh ibn ‘Ubadah narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah say that the Messenger of Allah forbade this, with a report like it, except that he did not mention dates at the end.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: I recited to Malik, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah said: “The two parties to a sale each have the option regarding the other as long as they have not separated, except in a sale in which the option is stipulated.”

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Yahya, al-Qattan, narrated to us; Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us; Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us. All reported from ‘Ubayd Allah, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, from the Prophet. Zuhayr and ‘Ali ibn Hujr narrated to me: Isma‘il narrated to us; Abu al-Rabi‘ and Abu Kamil narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us. Both reported from Ayyub, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, from the Prophet. Ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Abi ‘Umar narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, who said he heard Yahya ibn Sa‘id; and Ibn Rafi‘ narrated to us: Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us, from al-Dahhak. They all reported from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, from the Prophet, with a report like Malik’s from Nafi‘.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Rumh informed us: al-Layth informed us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, from the Messenger of Allah, who said: “When two men make a sale, each has the option as long as they remain together, unless one gives the other the choice. If one gives the other the choice and they make the sale on that basis, it becomes binding. If they separate after making the sale and neither cancels it, the sale is binding.”

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Ibn Abi ‘Umar narrated it to me, both from Sufyan—Zuhayr said Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to us—from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Nafi‘ dictated to me that he heard ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar say the Messenger of Allah said: “When buyer and seller make a sale, each has the option regarding the sale as long as they have not separated, or unless the sale is made with an option. If it is made with an option, it becomes binding.” Ibn Abi ‘Umar adds that Nafi‘ used to make a sale with a man and, if he wanted to ensure the man could not cancel it, he would stand and walk a little, then return to him.

Yahya ibn Yahya, Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us. Yahya ibn Yahya said: Isma‘il ibn Ja‘far informed us; the others said: Isma‘il narrated to us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Dinar, who heard Ibn ‘Umar say the Messenger of Allah said: “Each of the two parties to a sale has no binding sale between them until they separate, except a sale with an option.”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Yahya ibn Sa‘id narrated to us, from Shu‘bah; and ‘Amr ibn ‘Ali narrated to us: Yahya ibn Sa‘id and ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Shu‘bah, from Qatadah, from Abu al-Khalil, from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Hakim ibn Hizam, from the Prophet, who said: “The two parties to a sale have the option as long as they have not separated. If they are truthful and make everything clear, their sale is blessed; if they lie and conceal, the blessing of their sale is erased.”

‘Amr ibn ‘Ali narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us: Hammam narrated to us, from Abu al-Tayyah, who said: I heard ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Harith narrating from Hakim ibn Hizam, from the Prophet, with a report like it. Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj said: Hakim ibn Hizam was born inside the Ka‘bah and lived one hundred and twenty years.

Yahya ibn Yahya, Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us. Yahya ibn Yahya said: Isma‘il ibn Ja‘far informed us; the others said: Isma‘il narrated to us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Dinar, who heard Ibn ‘Umar say: A man told the Messenger of Allah that he was being cheated in sales. The Messenger said: “When you make a sale, say: ‘There is to be no deception.’” The man used to say, “No deception,” whenever he made a sale.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki‘ narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us; and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us. Both reported from ‘Abd Allah ibn Dinar with this chain and a report like it, but their reports do not include that he used to say, “No deception,” when making a sale.
Yahya ibn Yahya said: I recited to Malik, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah forbade selling fruit until its ripeness became apparent. He forbade both seller and buyer.
Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: ‘Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, from the Prophet, with a report like it.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Jarir narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said the Messenger of Allah said: “Do not buy fruit until its ripeness appears and the danger of blight has passed.” He said its ripeness appears through its redness or yellowness.
Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Abi ‘Umar narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, from Yahya, with this chain, up to “until its ripeness appears,” without mentioning what follows.
Ibn Rafi‘ narrated to us: Ibn Abi Fudayk informed us: al-Dahhak narrated to us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, from the Prophet, with a report like ‘Abd al-Wahhab’s.
Suwayd ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Hafs ibn Mayसरah narrated to us: Musa ibn ‘Uqbah narrated to me, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, from the Prophet, with a report like Malik’s and ‘Ubayd Allah’s.

Yahya ibn Yahya, Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us. Yahya said: Isma‘il, Ibn Ja‘far, informed us; the others said: he narrated to us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Dinar, who heard Ibn ‘Umar say the Messenger of Allah said: “Do not sell fruit until its ripeness appears.”

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated it to me: ‘Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan; and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us. Both reported from ‘Abd Allah ibn Dinar with this chain. Shu‘bah’s hadith adds that Ibn ‘Umar was asked what ripeness meant, and he replied: “When its blight has gone.”

Yahya ibn Yahya informed us: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to us, from al-Zuhri; and Ibn Numayr and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us—and the wording is theirs—from Sufyan, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Prophet forbade selling fruit until its ripeness appeared and selling fruit for dates.

‘Ali ibn Hujr al-Sa‘di and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Isma‘il narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah forbade selling dates until they had ripened and grain until it had whitened and was safe from blight. He forbade both seller and buyer.

Yahya ibn Yahya informed us: Abu Khaythamah narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir; and Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah forbade—or forbade us—from selling fruit until it had become good.

Ahmad ibn ‘Uthman al-Nawfali narrated to us: Abu ‘Asim narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me—and the wording is his—Rawh narrated to us. Both reported to us from Zakariyya ibn Ishaq, from ‘Amr ibn Dinar, who heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah say the Messenger of Allah forbade selling fruit until its ripeness appeared.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Numayr, and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from ‘Ata’, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah forbade muhaqalah, muzabanah, mukhabarah, and selling fruit until its ripeness appeared. It must not be sold except for dinars and dirhams, except for ‘araya.

‘Abd ibn Humayd informed us: Abu ‘Asim informed us: Ibn Jurayj informed us, from ‘Ata’ and Abu al-Zubayr, who both heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah say that the Messenger of Allah forbade these practices, with a report like it.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali informed us: Makhlad ibn Yazid al-Jazari narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us: ‘Ata’ informed me, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, that the Messenger of Allah forbade mukhabarah, muhaqalah, muzabanah, and selling fruit until it was fit to eat. It was not to be sold except for dirhams and dinars, except for ‘araya. ‘Ata’ said: Jabir explained to us: Mukhabarah is when a man gives another bare land to cultivate, the latter invests in it, then takes a share of the fruit. Muzabanah is selling fresh dates still on the palm for a measured amount of dried dates. Muhaqalah in crops is similar: selling standing crops for a measured amount of grain.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Khalaf both reported from Zakariyya. Ibn Abi Khalaf said: Zakariyya ibn ‘Adi narrated to us: ‘Ubayd Allah informed us, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah. Abu al-Walid al-Makki, while sitting with ‘Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah, narrated to us from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah that the Messenger of Allah forbade muhaqalah, muzabanah, mukhabarah, and buying date palms until they ripened—when they redden or yellow, or some of them can be eaten. Muhaqalah is selling a field for a known measure of food; muzabanah is selling date palms for measured loads of dates; mukhabarah is cultivating for a third, a fourth, or similar shares. Zayd said: I asked ‘Ata’ whether he heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah report this from the Messenger of Allah. He said, “Yes.”
